urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.name: Juveniles: Convictions and other types of conflict resolution
urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.description:
This dataset presents the annual figures for minor convictions and other types of conflict resolution by the offence, the criminal authority (cantonal court), the characteristics of the convicted person [sex, age, citizenship (Swiss or foreign by residence status)] and the decision year, since 2020.

The minor convictions for the years 1999 - 2019 are available in table form on our website under : Convictions of juveniles

A judgement may mention several offences, the sum of the various provisions is greater than the total.

Convictions pronounced against minors are only considered once the judgement comes into effect. The processing of possible appeals may, however, take some time and if the conviction is affirmed it is recorded under the date of first instance. For this reason, especially for serious crimes, it may take longer for all pronounced judgements of a given year to appear in the statistics. Furthermore, the time series for recent years are not relevant with regard to serious offences; it cannot be assumed that the figures are already complete.

A judgement may mention several offences, the sum of the various provisions is greater than the total.

urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.name: Persons convicted of a crime or offence under the Swiss Criminal Code (SCC) by nationality, offence, population category and year of conviction
urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.description:
This dataset presents the annual figures for adults convicted of a crime or offence under the Swiss Criminal Code (SCC), by nationality, offence and population category (permanent resident population in Switzerland or other population categories), since 2024.

The statistics on adult convictions (SUS) is based on judgements recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions. Convictions are only recorded once the judgement comes into effect. The processing of possible appeals may, however, take several years and if the conviction is affirmed it is recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions under the date of first instance.
For this reason, especially for serious crimes, several years may be necessary for all pronounced judgements of a given year to be recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions and to appear in the statistics. Furthermore, the time series for recent years are not relevant with regard to serious offences; it cannot be assumed that the figures are already complete.

Permanent resident population:
The permanent resident population includes all Swiss nationals with their main residence in Switzerland, foreign nationals with a residence or settlement permit for at least twelve months (permit B or C or FDFA identity card [international officials, diplomats and their family members]), foreign nationals with a short-term residence permit (L permit) for a cumulative period of at least twelve months, and persons in the asylum process (F, N or S permit) with a total period of residence of at least twelve months.

Conviction rates:
To calculate conviction rates for the permanent resident population, the number of persons of a given nationality convicted during a given year is divided by the number of persons of the same nationality residing in Switzerland at the end of the year (Source: Population and Household Statistics – STATPOP). This relative figure is multiplied by 100 to indicate how many out of 100 persons from the population with the same characteristics (nationality, age, gender) were convicted. This calculation is only performed for persons who are part of the permanent resident population.

urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.name: Adults: Convictions with prohibitions from carrying on an activity, contact prohibitions and exclusion orders
urn:sdmx:org.sdmx.infomodel.datastructur.description:
This dataset presents the annual figures of prohibitions from carrying on an activity, contact prohibitions and exclusion orders imposed on adults by criminal authority (cantonal, federal or military court), type of prohibition, characteristics of the convicted person [gender, age, citizenship (Swiss or foreigner depending on residence status)], since 2007.

Prohibitions from carrying on an activity, contact prohibitions and exclusion orders are ‘other measures’ within the meaning of the second section of the General Part of the Criminal Code (Art. 67 ff. SCC). Several prohibitions may be imposed in the same judgment.

The statistics on adult convictions (SUS) is based on judgements recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions. Convictions are only recorded once the judgement comes into effect. The processing of possible appeals may, however, take several years and if the conviction is affirmed it is recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions under the date of first instance.
For this reason, especially for serious crimes, several years may be necessary for all pronounced judgements of a given year to be recorded in the Register of Criminal Convictions and to appear in the statistics. Furthermore, the time series for recent years are not relevant with regard to serious offences; it cannot be assumed that the figures are already complete.
